concepts.quote: if (arr[i] == key) return i; else return -1;
concepts.why: Uses correct two-way if-else syntax, but the else returns -1 on the first mismatch so the loop never reaches a later (or last) match; the new code is wrong, so no L2-L4 credit, yet no rule contradicting Java is stated.
Correctly forms an array access with an int loop index, but the loop header is elided and no trace or bounds reasoning is given.
Writes a valid boolean comparison of an int element with a double key as the if condition, with no evaluation or type reasoning shown.
Names a for loop as the traversal construct but leaves the header empty, and the body returns on every first pass so the loop cannot scan for the last occurrence; no header rule is applied.
